actions.title: Build and ship a tool for a real group you belong to
actions.description: Find a manual process in a society, sports club or part-time job and replace it with a small web app that people actually use. Keep it running.
actions.evidence: Live link + public GitHub repo; README states the problem, stack, who uses it and one outcome (e.g. users, time saved), honestly measured. Add one fact someone else can check: number of users, sessions or issues filed by other people.

sources.quote: You could look at sports clubs, groups and societies you already belong to and see if they have any processes or databases you could improve

actions.title: Turn a tutorial project into one that solves your own problem
actions.description: Use a tutorial only as a starting point: change it so it solves a problem you or a named group actually have, add tests and CI, and write a short 'what I'd change next' note. Treat it as a stepping stone to a project with real users (see 'Build and ship a tool for a real group'), not a headline project: AI tools make tutorial-style code cheap to produce.
actions.evidence: Repo with passing CI, a live demo, and README sections 'What problem this solves for whom' and 'What I'd change next' (addresses SWE-17a: unextended tutorial clones).

sources.quote: If you were self-taught, then yes! Or if you’ve used that skill to solve a problem, yes again!

actions.title: Write a design note for your best project
actions.description: One page covering the architecture, two alternatives you rejected and why, known limitations, and what you would do with more time. Rehearse explaining it in 3 minutes.

yearGuidance.1st: Ship 1-2 small projects with a README and GitHub link, go to a hackathon, and start light coding-interview practice. Few big-tech firms run first-year internships now; bank technology spring insights (for students graduating in 2029; JPMorganChase allows one Spring Insights application) and trading-firm programmes such as Jane Street FTTP are the main first-year routes.
yearGuidance.2nd: Your stage depends on your course. Three-year degree: you're penultimate, so apply for summer internships in the autumn. Four-year integrated master's (MEng/MSci): spring weeks and insight programmes are often still open to you, and you can try a first summer internship. Degree with a placement year: the autumn of your second year is your main application season, as 12-month placements open around September and big employers fill early.
yearGuidance.penultimate: Apply for summer internships or placements early in the autumn: many tech firms open in August–September, close by November and make offers on a rolling basis. Expect a timed coding test first, so practise data structures and algorithms before applying. Have 2-4 projects with stack and outcome, and a design note you can talk through.
yearGuidance.final: Graduate schemes open around September to November, and many close by December or fill on a rolling basis. Lead with internship or strongest project, add your final-year project, keep GitHub current, and keep coding-test practice going.
yearGuidance.masters: On a one-year MSc, apply in your first 6-8 weeks: employers see your undergraduate CV plus your MSc modules. Make the dissertation or project a headline item with results.

yearGuidance.1st: Protect your grades; make one analysis reproducible; write a short literature review; start conversations with academics. In the biosciences, find out now which supervisors could back a summer vacation studentship in your second year.
yearGuidance.2nd: Seek a summer research project (UROP-style) or a learned-society vacation studentship (Microbiology Society opens in December; the Biochemical Society in late February). Reproduce a published result.
yearGuidance.penultimate: Apply for funded summer research (e.g. LMS bursary for maths/stats); present a poster if possible.
yearGuidance.final: Make the dissertation your headline research experience; line up academic referees.
yearGuidance.masters: Research project + any posters/preprints, cited honestly (RES-04); apply for PhD or research roles.
